speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the consultation. I understand you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; have you noticed if the vomit is green or yellow in color? Additionally, has your abdomen appeared distended or swollen since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intestinal Malrotation with Midgut Volvulus. The presence of bilious vomiting in a newborn born at term, combined with the family history of pyloric stenosis (suggesting a genetic predisposition to gastrointestinal motility or obstruction issues), is highly concerning for malrotation with volvulus, a surgical emergency. Immediate surgical consultation is required.
